messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] high tail latency detected for tenant=CobaltHealth (dedicated-vpc-eu-west). p99 gen latency jumped to 3.2s, queue_len=120, GPU_util=94% :rotating_light:

alex: paging oncall — looks like a surge from a customer-side loop. their queue is dominating the scheduler, pushing others into timeouts.

marta: seeing same metrics on the dashboard. their bespoke pool has one shard with continuous high backlog. p50 180ms, p95 1.1s, p99 3.2s. requests/sec spiked x12 on their routes.

chris: any recent deploys for CobaltHealth?

alex: not from our side. they rolled a new agent earlier today but no deploy on our infra. probable workload change.

jamie: can we quick-isolate them into a shaped queue? we can apply a temporary max_batch_tokens cap and lower scheduler weight.

sre-oncall: agree. plan: (1) reduce tenant scheduler weight to 0.2, (2) set max_batch_tokens=2048 for tenant, (3) enable queue_shaper mode "fair_share" for that pool.

marta: if we cap max_batch_tokens higher we'll still get large batches — I think we should actually reduce to 512 for now so one large request doesn't block many small ones.

alex: good call. small requests are what other customers hit. I'm going to run the change. preparing command.

alex: running:
```
# apply per-tenant scheduler knobs
tenantsctl set --tenant CobaltHealth --scheduler.weight 0.2 --scheduler.queue_shaper fair_share --serving.max_batch_tokens 512
```

incident-bot: change-request logged (change-id: CHG-87321). awaiting enforcement.

chris: logs show enforcement on shard-8 now. queue_len for CobaltHealth dropped from 120 -> 28 within 45s. GPU_util on shard-8 down to 78%.

jamie: nice, p99 trending down to ~1.4s. still above SLO but much better.

marta: observed side-effect: batch formation rate decreased, so overall throughput for CobaltHealth dropped by ~25%. need to confirm they accept degraded throughput.

alex: looped in account team: @marta can you ping their AE to let them know we applied a temporary mitigation?

marta: pinged via DM — AE said they saw errors earlier and are willing to accept throttling while we triage. asked for a postmortem once stable.

sre-oncall: also enabling prefix caching for their most common prompt prefixes to reduce repeated KV overhead. applying a quick cache rule:
```
cachectl add-rule --tenant CobaltHealth --prefix "PatientSummary:" --ttl 600
```

chris: cache hit rate improved from 2% -> 18% on those routes. p95 further down to 850ms.

jamie: can we schedule a canary rollback of the scheduler knobs in 30m if stable? want to avoid prolonged customer impact.

alex: yes. setting automated rollback job: if p99 < 900ms and queue_len < 20 for 10m, revert to prior scheduler.weight/ max_batch_tokens.

incident-bot: automated rollback scheduled (job-id: RBK-449). will evaluate metrics at T+30m.

marta: heads-up: we saw a secondary spike from a background batch job on CobaltHealth that sends very long-generation requests at 03:00 UTC. recommend we coordinate with their infra to smooth that cadence.

alex: noted. adding follow-up action item to incident ticket.

sre-oncall: handoff: I'm going to step out in 10m — @chris you'll own monitoring and execute rollback if conditions met. if p99 rises again, escalate to infra-contacts and we may isolate the tenant to a dedicated isolated shard.

chris: got it. will monitor dashboard and traces. set alerts on queue_len>25 and p99>1.5s.

jamie: creating incident ticket with timeline, configs changed, and next steps. tagging product and account teams.

marta: account team confirmed they're disabling the background batch job as a temporary action to help. they also committed to a rate-limit on their agent.

alex: quick note for postmortem: evaluate whether we need an automatic tenant-level token bucket that gates large token requests during sustained backlog. maybe a dynamic max_batch_tokens that decays when queue grows.

chris: agree — I can prototype a greedy_decay knob: max_batch_tokens = base * (1 - alpha * queue_ratio).

sre-oncall: good idea. create an RFC for scheduler adaptive knobs and include a safety circuit that never drops below 128 tokens.

incident-bot: RBK-449 triggered at 2098765692: p99=740ms, queue_len=12 -> rollback applied by automation.

alex: rollback completed. max_batch_tokens restored to 4096 and scheduler.weight back to 1.0 for CobaltHealth.

marta: monitoring post-rollback for 15m. p99 steady ~700ms, GPU_util normalized.

jamie: closing on-call actions: document change commands, contact logs, and AE confirmation. will escalate to infra for adaptive scheduler RFC.

chris: leaving note for follow-up: timeline + graphs saved in INCIDENT-2026-04-CobaltHealth.

sre-oncall: handing off to day team for follow-up and postmortem. oncall clear from my side.

alex: thanks team. tagging participants for postmortem: @marta @chris @jamie @sre-oncall.

marta: thanks — will draft postmortem and share with account.

incident-bot: incident status -> RESOLVED (duration: 14m).
